follow_up.reference: The cash previously earned interest in the standalone forecast. Spending it removes that interest income, so the transaction must cover this opportunity cost even without new borrowing.

instances.text: A client compares a cash purchase with remaining standalone. The buyer has annual standalone net income of 150 million dollars and 100 million common shares. It pays 1100 million dollars entirely from existing cash to buy a target earning 140 million dollars after tax annually. The spent cash previously earned 5 percent pre-tax, already included in buyer earnings. Interest income is taxed at 40 percent. Assume a start-of-year close, no borrowing, no new shares, no synergies, no fees and no purchase-accounting charges. What is full-year pro forma EPS, in dollars per share?
